newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil unions hold new talks with Cosipa on strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil unions hold new talks with Cosipa on strike.

text.p: Brazilian stevedore representatives will meet the chairman of steel company Cosipa for further talks to resolve a strike at Santos port which will become national on Friday, an union official said.
The meeting will take place at 1400 local/1700 GMT, probably at the same location in Sao Paulo where initial talks were held Tuesday, the spokesman said.

Aldo Narcise, chairman of the board of Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa), will meet Abelardo Fernandes, president of the National Stevedores' Union, and Joaquim da Silva, president of the Santos Stevedores' Union.
Cosipa repeated that the talks were a personal initiative and, officially, it was not holding any meetings with the unions.
"These talks are being held at the request of Sao Paulo Labor Secretary Walter Barelli," a Cosipa spokeswoman said.
Workers at Santos began an indefinite strike at 0700 local Tuesday in protest against Cosipa using its own workers to load and unload vessels at its private terminal at Santos.
Stevedores said it would widen to a 48-hour national stoppage starting Friday unless a solution to the conflict was found.
